epistemic_assessments.rationale: No supplied source establishes what obligation, decision or external requirement set the four-contact threshold. Three periodic reviews record 'no change' and the pre-v4 history was not migrated.
epistemic_assessments.question_asked: What obligation, decision or external requirement established the four-contact cap in Standard CC-11?
epistemic_assessments.scope_searched: standard-cc-11 v6 and its recorded document history; collections operating manual 2025 section 4.2; Ashcombe design note v3; exception register 2025; TDA and risk forum minutes 2025-09 to 2026-02.

epistemic_assessments.rationale: standard-cc-11 v6 is a live standard, reviewed 2023-11-04, and states the cap.

payload.statement: The four-contact cap in Standard CC-11 is in force and enforced as a hard constraint by the Ashcombe engine, and its originating authority cannot be located in the supplied estate.
payload.scope: Standard CC-11, and the Ashcombe contact strategy engine that enforces it.
recommended_next_evidence: Pre-2021 versions of Standard CC-11 or its predecessor
Any committee minute or supervisory correspondence introducing a contact cap
The migration record explaining what pre-v4 history was not carried forward

required_authority: None to record the finding. Any change to CC-11 would require the authority that set it, which is precisely what is UNKNOWN.
caveat: An unlocated origin is not an absent one. The Bank's own design note records the same gap independently.
prohibited_inference: That the cap is internal, discretionary or removable
That 'periodic review, no change' evidences origin
That the Head of Collections, who may grant exceptions, set the rule
